stills.style: A single hand-made illustration on white paper in which ONE figure is drawn in many different art mediums at once, like a patchwork: her figure is divided into about ten irregular patches with soft torn-paper seams between them, and each patch is rendered in a different medium: opaque gouache paint; coloured pencil hatching; woodblock print with bold black key lines; fine pen-and-ink stippling; thin plotter lines on pale green graph paper; sumi ink wash; airbrush; two-colour risograph halftone dots; square 16-bit pixel art; wax crayon; and white-line scratchboard on black. The outline of her figure is continuous and correct through every patch: it is one drawing of one woman, not a collage of different people.
stills.scene: She stands three-quarter length, from the knees up, in the centre of the picture, calm, arms relaxed and slightly open at her sides, palms forward, looking straight at the viewer with her eyes open. Her face is divided by only one seam, running down beside her nose, so that both eyes, the brows, the nose and the mouth stay clear and are exactly her features in both halves; the other patches cover her hair, jacket, arms, top and trousers. Each patch carries a little of its own colour: rose pink, golden yellow, coral red, mint green, cyan, magenta, blue, violet, with orange for the bands of her jacket. The background is plain white paper with only faint pencil construction lines.

A flat cel-shaded anime drawing with a clean inked line, drawn on black paper: flat colours, no gradients, no glow, no 3D; light drawn as hand-made strokes of golden pencil. A very wide view from high up at the back of a concert stage, looking down over a full symphony orchestra from BEHIND the players toward the front of the stage. Every single player is the same woman, the woman of the reference sheet, seen from behind: long straight black hair to the waist, a white cropped bomber jacket whose plain white back carries only a large pale-blue circle (no stripe or band across the back), wide navy trousers. About eighty of her sit in the standard seating of a symphony orchestra in curved rows around the podium: first violins at the front on the left of the stage and second violins beside them, violas in the middle, cellos at the front on the right with double basses standing behind them, flutes, oboes, clarinets and bassoons in two rows in the centre, horns, trumpets, trombones and a tuba behind them, timpani and percussion at the very back nearest the viewer, a harp at the left and a grand piano at the left edge. The instruments are drawn in warm gold and brown pencil; everything else is white, navy and black. So the picture is rows and rows of white jacket backs with pale-blue circles, bows all at the same angle. At the front of the stage, beyond the orchestra and facing it, where a conductor would stand, a line of seven of the same woman are not playing: they hold a low wushu bow stance in perfect unison, one arm punched forward, and the one in the centre stands on the podium. Beyond them the hall is empty black paper. Wide 16:9 picture that fills the frame, no border, no caption, no text.
